en: The Therāpadāna, Yasavagga 1. The Apadāna of the Elder Yaśas [Verse 1] When the Great Sage was dwelling in the city of Bandhumatī, I was a merchant’s son there, named Yaśas. [Verse 2] At that time, the Teacher, the Buddha, went forth from home into homelessness; Having renounced his kingdom, he became a monk for the sake of awakening. [Verse 3] Then I, having heard of the Teacher’s departure, Filled with joy, approached the Blessed One. [Verse 4] Having approached him, I paid homage at his feet, And sat down to one side before the Teacher. [Verse 5] Seated there, I spoke these words to the Buddha: “O Sage, please accept me as a lay follower. [Verse 6] The Teacher, knowing my intention, Out of compassion for me, accepted me. [Verse 7] Having become a lay follower, I took refuge in the Triple Gem, And thereafter I practiced the five precepts. [Verse 8] For twenty thousand years I lived as a lay follower, And during that time I never committed any evil deed. [Verse 9] When the Teacher had passed away, the Dharma remained, And I continued to practice the holy life under the Dharma. [Verse 10] When the Dharma had passed away, the Saṅgha remained, And I continued to honor the Saṅgha with offerings. [Verse 11] For twenty thousand years I honored the Saṅgha, And through that merit I attained rebirth in heaven. [Verse 12] In the heavenly world I enjoyed divine pleasures, And after passing from there, I was reborn among humans. [Verse 13] In every birth I was born into a noble family, Possessing great wealth and abundant grain. [Verse 14] I was always handsome and possessed of splendor, And my fame spread throughout the four quarters. [Verse 15] Because of that root of goodness, I have now attained this state, Having abandoned all defilements, I have realized Nibbāna. [Verse 16] I have fulfilled the training and am established in the fruit; I have reached the goal and am free from all suffering. [Verse 17] This is my final birth; no further existence shall I take, Having crossed over the flood, I have reached the further shore. [Verse 18] I have seen the end of birth and death; My holy life has been lived, and what was to be done has been done. [Verse 19] I have attained the peace of Nibbāna, cool and blissful; I am a sage who has laid down the heavy burden. [Verse 20] I have no more future births; I have reached the goal and am free from all suffering. [Verse 21] Thus did the Elder Yaśas speak of his own past deeds; Having heard this, one should strive to emulate his conduct.
“Having plunged into the great ocean,
my abode was well-constructed;
the lotus pond was well-constructed.”
Resounding with the cries of ruddy geese,
it was covered with mandārava flowers as well as lotuses and water lilies.
And there a river flows,
with beautiful banks, delightful,
and covered with fish and turtles.
It resounds with the cries of various birds,
echoing with the calls of peacocks and herons,
and the sweet songs of cuckoos and other warblers.
Doves, sun-birds, ruddy geese, river-dwellers,
partridges, and sparrows are there as well.
Pāvaka birds, jīvañjīvaka birds;
swans and cranes crying out,
many kosiya and piṅgala birds.
Endowed with the seven treasures— gems,
pearls, and coral—
all the trees were made of gold.
Stirred by various elements,
they illuminate the abode at all times, day and night.
Sixty thousand musical instruments resounded morning and evening,
and sixteen thousand women—
They always surround me.
Having gone forth from my abode,
[I saw] Sumedha, the Leader of the World.
With a clear mind and joyful heart,
I paid homage to that one of great renown;
having saluted the Perfectly Enlightened One, I—
I invited him along with the Saṅgha;
that wise one, Sumedha, the Leader of the World, accepted.
Having delivered a discourse on the Dhamma,
the Great Sage dismissed him;
having paid homage to the Fully Enlightened One, [he departed].
I approached my dwelling and addressed my attendants:
"Let everyone assemble then."
‘In the morning, the Buddha will come to our dwelling.
It is a gain for us, it is well-acquired by us!’
"Since we dwell in your presence,
we too shall pay homage to the Teacher, the Supreme Buddha."
Having prepared food and drink,
I announced the time [for the meal] together with one hundred thousand masters (vasīs).
The Leader of the World approached.
I went out to meet him with music provided by the fivefold orchestra.
The Supreme Person sat upon a throne made entirely of gold;
there was a canopy above.
Then, made entirely of gold,
fans were fanned over the unsurpassed Saṅgha of bhikkhus.
I satisfied the community of monks with abundant food and drink,
and with pairs of individual garments.
I gave it to the community of monks.
That which Sumedha declares is the recipient of offerings.
Having sat down in the community of bhikkhus,
he spoke these verses:
"Whoever [serves] me with food and drink..."
And he satisfied them all;
I shall praise him,
so listen as I speak.
In eighteen hundred kappas,
he will delight in the world of the gods;
a thousand times he will be a king.
He will become a wheel-turning monarch.
Whatever womb he enters—
whether that of a deity or a human—
Its covering will consist entirely of gold for thirty thousand eons.
Born of the Okkāka clan,
he will be a teacher in the world named Gotama by lineage.
His heir in the Dhammas,
his own legitimate son, fashioned by the Dhamma;
having fully understood all taints,
Free from taints, he will attain Nibbāna.
Seated within the community of bhikkhus,
he will roar the lion’s roar.
They hold a parasol over you;
stay beneath the parasol!
I have attained the state of a recluse.
The defilements have been burnt away by me;
whether in a pavilion or at the foot of a tree,
no fear exists for me.
In the thirty thousand aeons during which I gave that gift,
I do not recall ever being born in an unhappy state.
This is the fruit of all my giving:
my defilements have been incinerated,
and all states of existence have been uprooted.
Like a snake that has severed its bonds,
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me!
In the presence of my Buddha,
the three knowledges have been attained;
the teaching of the Buddha has been accomplished.
The four analytical knowledges,
these eight liberations,
and the six direct knowledges have been realized.
“Such is the teaching of the Buddha.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder Yasa speak these verses.
This is the first legend of the Elder Yasa.
